preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner (or gain control of owner account)
Attacker must hold some amount of the token to perform a sell transaction

violation_target.exploit_hint: As the contract owner, call setBuyTaxes() or setSelTaxes() to set extremely high fees (e.g., 99% each). Then perform a sell transaction through the Uniswap pair. The high fees will cause most of the token sale proceeds to be distributed to marketing and team wallets (which the attacker controls), while the attacker receives minimal tokens. The contract will swap tokens for ETH and transfer ETH to the attacker-controlled wallets, resulting in financial gain.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The TokenTool contract has owner-only functions to set extremely high buy/sell taxes (up to 99%). The owner can also change the marketing and team wallet addresses. By setting high sell taxes and controlling the fee recipient wallets, the owner can extract value from users selling tokens. When a user sells, most of the proceeds go to the marketing/team wallets as ETH, which the attacker controls.
attempts.attack_strategy: Impersonate the owner, set 99% sell taxes, change fee recipient wallets to attacker addresses, acquire tokens, sell them through Uniswap, and collect the ETH fees sent to attacker-controlled wallets.
attempts.step_by_step_plan:
1. Impersonate the contract owner using vm.prank
2. Set sell taxes to 99% total using setSelTaxes(33, 33, 33)
3. Change marketing and team wallets to attacker addresses
4. Get tokens from owner (transfer to attacker)
5. Approve Uniswap router to spend tokens
6. Sell tokens via swapExactTokensForETHSupportingFeeOnTransferTokens
7. Collect ETH from marketing/team wallets
